title: Distributed Message Queue
summary: Build a durable distributed queue with competing consumers, redelivery and isolated poison messages.
narrative:
The Client here is the producer service, and Workers are the consumers. Build an SQS/RabbitMQ-like service with send, receive and ack/delete operations. A received message is hidden by a visibility timeout, then becomes eligible for redelivery if the consumer fails to acknowledge it. Competing consumers share the work: one consumer handles a delivery at a time, but at-least-once delivery means retries can produce duplicates, so consumers must make side effects idempotent.

Route producers through a Load Balancer to Message Queue broker nodes. Shard queues across the broker fleet and replicate each queue as a quorum queue, acknowledging a send only after durable replication. Broker redundancy and per-queue replication are distinct: a production quorum normally uses an odd replica set such as three members to retain a majority after one failure. Use ZooKeeper/etcd as the membership, queue-leadership and metadata control plane; producers learn queue behavior through brokers rather than contacting that coordinator.

Run multiple consumers and move a message to a Dead Letter Queue after N unsuccessful attempts, preserving failure details for inspection and controlled redrive. Track queue depth, oldest-message age and redelivery rates with optional Monitoring. A queue distributes a message among competing consumers; pub/sub gives each subscription a copy. An optional Pub/Sub fan-out exchange can route copies into separate subscriber queues hosted on the brokers, with competing Workers inside each queue. Producers never invoke Workers directly.

functional: Send messages, receive them with a visibility timeout, and ack/delete successful deliveries
Shard queues across brokers and replicate each queue before acknowledging durable sends
Distribute deliveries among competing Workers and retry unacknowledged messages
Move poison messages to a Dead Letter Queue after N unsuccessful attempts
Maintain broker membership, queue leadership and metadata through ZooKeeper/etcd
nonFunctional: Scale broker throughput and consumer concurrency independently
Preserve accepted messages through broker failures using quorum replication
Use idempotent consumer side effects to tolerate duplicate delivery
constraints: Producer-to-consumer paths must pass through a Message Queue
Producers must not call Workers or ZooKeeper/etcd directly
Keep coordination metadata separate from message payloads
capacity: Partition queues across broker nodes as send/receive throughput grows
Choose visibility timeout from processing duration; move messages after N failed attempts
Use a majority-based replica set per queue; three replicas normally tolerate one failed member
specs.tradeoff: At-least-once delivery favors durability over duplicate-free side effects. Longer visibility timeouts reduce premature retries but delay recovery after a consumer dies; competing consumers scale work while sacrificing a single global completion order.
specs.bonus: Route Load Balancer → Pub/Sub → Message Queue for a fan-out exchange and add Monitoring for backlog and delivery failures.

resilienceRules.message: Run at least two broker nodes and replicate queues so one broker is not the only host.
Run at least two Workers so consumption can continue when one fails.
Connect queue brokers to a Dead Letter Queue for poison messages.
Connect brokers to ZooKeeper/etcd for membership and queue leadership.

hints: Start with Client → Load Balancer → Message Queue → Worker. The Client produces messages and the Worker consumes them; the queue owns visibility timeout and acknowledgement state.
Connect Message Queue → Dead Letter Queue for messages that exhaust retries and → ZooKeeper/etcd for membership and leadership. Keep both the coordinator and consumers behind brokers.

Use two Message Queues and two Workers: balance to both brokers and connect each broker to both Workers, the DLQ and ZooKeeper/etcd. Add Load Balancer → Pub/Sub → both brokers for fan-out and connect both brokers to Monitoring.
